Alex.feeling: Murky: Casey's and Blair's stories keep shifting, and the Eagle and Turkey counts are hard to reconcile. The table is converging, but I'm not fully sure of the throw.

Blair.feeling: Messy and tense: Casey's Eagle count keeps not adding up, and I made an early misstatement about my Turkey that I had to correct on the record.

Casey.feeling: Messy and frustrating: the claims keep contradicting each other, and my own Eagle count is being questioned even though I think it checks out.

Drew.feeling: Tense and muddled: the Eagle, Turkey, and Owl claims keep contradicting each other, and I'm hiding as a Meowfia Floofer while pretending to be the Hawk.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and frustrating: Casey's and Blair's egg stories keep contradicting each other, and I'm not fully sure who is lying.

Finley.feeling: Murky and tense: the Eagle and Turkey egg counts keep conflicting, and as the Meowfia Sphinx I have to stay quiet about my own visit while steering the vote.

Alex.note: Most of the table is on Casey, and Casey's egg count doesn't add up. I'll throw two lower cards at Casey and keep my high cards.

Blair.note: I'm Farm, and Casey's Eagle count doesn't add up with the Turkey egg, so Casey is the likely Meowfia. I'll throw two lower cards at Casey to add votes and keep my two Kings.

Drew.note: Same plan: the table is converging on Casey, so I throw at Casey and bank high cards if Meowfia wins.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle and Turkey egg counting was hard to verify, since visitors to a Turkey and to an Eagle's own visit pay out differently. I also never got a clear answer on who the second visitor to Casey was.
Alex.fun: Round 1 went well: Blair's Sphinx claim and Ellis's Kookaburra story lined up with my Eagle count, and the table threw Blair out with a big consensus vote.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports name visitors more clearly, since Owl and Eagle reports only give animals and that made claims hard to check.
Alex.regret: In Round 2 I threw at Casey alongside the table without questioning Ellis's Falcon story, and Casey was actually Farm, so I would have checked Ellis's claim more before following the vote.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey and Eagle egg rules were easy to misread: I first said nobody visited my Turkey, when visitors actually paid me nothing and the Turkey pays the visitor. Several players also argued over whether a player's own visit counts toward an Eagle's total.
Blair.fun: As Sphinx in round 1, learning the full list of Farm roles and then watching the table argue over Alex's Eagle count was the most enjoyable part. Blair's Sphinx reveal drew a lot of pressure, and it was fun to see the whole table react to it.
Blair.change: I would make the Eagle and Turkey egg rules explicit in the dawn report, so players don't have to reason through who pays whom. I'd also make visitor counts easier to verify.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I wrongly said nobody visited my Turkey, which made me look like a liar until I corrected it. I should have checked my own rule first and simply said Finley visited me and paid the Turkey egg, and I should not have thrown at Casey, who was actually Farm, since it helped Meowfia win.

Casey.confusing: The Mouser's visit and how the Eagle counts visitors (whether my own visit to a player counted) were hard to pin down from the dawn reports alone. Turkey payouts also muddied Round 3.
Casey.fun: Round 2's Tit guess on Drew paid off as a confirmed Hawk, and watching the table argue over Alex's shifting Eagle and Owl claims was a good read game.
Casey.change: Have the dawn reports name each visitor when a role counts visitors, so Eagle and Owl claims can be checked instead of argued.
Casey.regret: In Round 3 I built the case against Blair, a Farm Turkey, and let Finley, the Meowfia Sphinx, go unchallenged; I would have pressed Finley's visit and role claim instead.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle counting rule was hard to pin down: it's unclear whether a visit by the Eagle to someone else, or a Turkey payout, should count toward the Eagle's own egg total. Blair's Turkey correction also muddied the day.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when Ellis's Kookaburra claim and my Hawk egg both pointed at Blair and the table converged on a correct read, that felt like a clean win. Round 3 was fun too, since I bluffed as a Hawk while actually being the Floofer.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since nobody can verify claims like Eagle or Turkey counts without the raw visit list.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I falsely claimed Hawk and cleared Finley, then helped throw at Casey, who was Farm. I'd have been better off keeping quiet and letting the Farm players argue among themselves.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle and Turkey egg counting was hard to pin down, since Blair's Turkey gave eggs to visitors and Casey's +2 depended on whether a player's own visit counted. Blair's "nobody visited me" correction also made the timing hard to follow.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 went cleanly: Ellis's Kookaburra visit to the Sphinx exposed Blair, and the whole table converged on the right throw.
Ellis.change: I'd make the dawn egg reports and role claims easier to check against each other, so a claim like "my nest went up by 2" can be verified against the visits listed.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I backed the throw at Casey on an Eagle count argument, when Casey was Farm and Finley, whose +1 I had accepted, was the Sphinx. I should have pressed Finley's visit and Drew's Hawk claim before throwing at a Farm player.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle and Turkey egg counting was hard to verify, since Blair's Turkey gave eggs to visitors and the Eagle counted visitors to itself, so nobody could cleanly check Casey's +2. Casey's Eagle claim was actually true, which I only learned now.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: Blair's Sphinx list matched my Owl claim, the table converged on Blair, and my two-card throw banked 11 points when Farm won.
Finley.change: I'd make the day's egg-count reports easier to cross-check, such as having the Storyteller state each visit publicly, so Eagle and Turkey claims can be verified without guessing.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw my Sphinx-claim-free vote at Blair, a true Farm Turkey, and kept the wrong read; I should have backed Casey's Eagle claim, which was true, and not pushed the table against it.

review.title: Two Farm Casualties
review.headline: Farm nailed Blair, then eggsecuted innocent Casey twice while Drew banked 42.
review.summary: Round 1 was a clean Farm win: Kookaburra, Hawk and Eagle claims all pointed at Blair the Sphinx. In rounds 2 and 3 the Farm table fixated on Casey, who was Farm both times, and Meowfia won both rounds. Drew, a Meowfia Floofer in round 3 with a large hand, banked 21 and won the game at 42.

rounds.recap: Ellis's Kookaburra read, Drew's Hawk egg and Alex's Eagle count all confirmed Blair as the Sphinx. Casey's Mouser claim looked bad, but the vote went to Blair and Farm won easily. Drew and Finley banked big.

Blair winked Drew, the confirmed Hawk, mid-day. Casey's Tit story, with an unexplained Wild egg, and Alex's Owl claim confused everyone. The table went after Casey, who was Farm, and Meowfia (Blair and Finley) won. Finley threw at Casey too, which helped his own side.

Blair misread his Turkey and said nobody visited him, then corrected it. Casey's Eagle count of +2 was argued over, and Casey was wrongly seen as the liar. Farm eggsecuted Casey, who was Farm. Meowfia Drew and Finley won, and Drew banked a 13 and an 8.

highlights.text: Three independent Farm claims (Kookaburra, Hawk, Eagle) converged on Blair, and Blair's honest Sphinx list sealed it.
Blair winked Drew, the confirmed Hawk and score leader, mid-day. Nobody learned who did it.
Finley, a Meowfia, threw one cheap card at Blair, a known Farm, while Drew led the crowd onto Casey.
The table argued for several beats over whether Casey's +2 included his own visit to Blair.

confusions.what: Said a Turkey only gains eggs when visited and that nobody visited him. A Turkey lays eggs in visitors' nests. He corrected this later.

Counted his own visit to Blair as a visitor for his Eagle gain. He also treated Eagle as giving eggs by visiting, when the egg lands in his own nest for each visitor to the target. His +2 was really one Finley visit plus the Turkey egg.
Claimed Owl but expected to name visitors. Owl only reveals animals. He also called the Hawk visit suspicious, even though Drew the Hawk visited Casey.
Accepted that Casey's own visit counted toward his Eagle +2, which is not how Eagle works.
Said Drew's Hawk with no egg did not fit because I was Meowfia. This was an intentional bluff, but it was a rules-confused argument. Drew's Hawk claim was a lie that no one could check.
Claimed Mouser while being truly Mouser, then repeated that Drew was Hawk. The table treated a true Meowfia claim as an obvious lie.

worked: Round 1 showed the cross-checking design well. Kookaburra, Hawk and Eagle reports could be verified against each other and led to a satisfying correct vote.
The Wink was a real decision. Blair used it on a confirmed Hawk and the table could not tell who did it.
Throw count as a signal and the consolation return made each throw a real choice. Finley's one-card throws were cheap and kept his high cards.
Floofer hugging the Hawk blanked Farm information in round 2 and made the Falcon and Owl reports harder to read.
problems: Eagle, Owl and Turkey wording confused nearly every player. Eagle gains eggs per visitor to its target, and Owl reports animals, not names. Add a short worked example, or reword the cards as who gains eggs.

The leader ran away. Drew banked 16 in round 1 and 21 in round 3. High cards thrown on the winning side score full value, so rich nests snowball. Cap banked value per round, or reduce the Kings' value.
Meowfia won two rounds by eggsecuting the same wrongly accused Farm player. Mixed claims and no reliable verification made Farm vote on noise. Give Farm a stronger source of verified information.

Meowfia don't know each other, but the Sphinx can learn the Farm roles, which lets them bluff convincingly with a full role list. Finley used this to pick a safe target. Consider weakening the Sphinx.

Players had no memory pressure across rounds. Alex and Casey were attacked for claiming different roles in different rounds, even though roles are re-dealt. Remind players of this, or hide previous-round roles.
